name: 3-Legged Dog
description: A beginner-friendly full-body yoga exercise that primarily targets the shoulders, core, and hips while improving hip mobility, enhancing spinal alignment, and building overall balance and stability.

form: Start in Three-Legged Downward Dog, with your hands firmly planted shoulder-width apart.
Bend your right knee, open your hip, and bring your right heel towards your glutes.

Press up rapidly with your calfs and extend your knees to lift onto the balls of your feet.
Lower back down at a slightly slower pace.

Roll your calf back and forth over the roller.
Apply pressure to tight spots.

Hold at the top for a moment.
Smoothly lower back to the ground.

proTips: Keep your neck in a neutral position.

name: Wide Push-Ups
description: An intermediate upper body push exercise that emphasizes the chest, shoulders, and triceps while helping to build pressing strength, enhance muscular endurance, and improve upper body stability.

form: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body until your elbows are at a 90° angle.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Press back up to the starting position.
proTips: Keep your back flat to maintain a neutral spine.
Ensure your movements are smooth and controlled.
commonMistakes: Don't let your head drop; keep your neck in line with your spine to maintain proper alignment.

name: Wild Thing
description: A beginner-friendly full-body exercise that primarily targets the shoulders, obliques, glutes, and core while improving spinal mobility, shoulder stability, and overall balance and coordination.

form: Start in a side plank.
Shift your weight onto your right hand as you pivot onto the outer edge of your right foot.
Float your left leg above the ground with the knee bent and the ball of your foot on the ground.
Lift your hips and open your chest toward the ceiling.
Extend your left arm overhead and back, reaching towards the floor behind you.
proTips: Engage your core to support your spine.
Extend your hips up and open your chest towards the ceiling.
commonMistakes: Avoid straining the neck by keeping it long and relaxed.

name: Wind-Releasing Pose
description: A beginner-friendly core and lower back exercise that gently targets the hip flexors and spinal muscles while helping to relieve lower back tension, improve digestion, and promote overall relaxation.

form: Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms by your sides.
Clasp your hands around your shins, hugging your knees into your chest.
Gently pull your nose towards your knees.
Hold the pose, breathing deeply to relax.
proTips: Breathe naturally, bringing your nose closer to your knees as you exhale.
Rest your hands on top of your shins or wrap them underneath if more comfortable.
commonMistakes: Pull towards the knees gently, avoid forcing or straining.

name: Wipers
description: A beginner-friendly core exercise that primarily targets the obliques and lower abdominals while improving spinal stability, enhancing rotational control, and building a stronger, more resilient midsection.

form: Lie on your back with your arms extended to the sides for stability.
Lift your legs to 90°, keeping them straight and together.
Engage your core and lower your legs to the right side, keeping your shoulders flat on the mat.
Bring your legs back to the center position using your core muscles.
With control, lower your legs to the left side. Continue alternating sides in a controlled, steady motion.
proTips: Focus on slow, deliberate movements to maximize core engagement.
For an easier variation, bend your knees.
commonMistakes: Don't let your shoulders lift off the mat; keep them grounded.

name: Wrist Rotations
description: A beginner-friendly forearm and wrist exercise that primarily targets the wrist flexors and extensors while improving joint mobility, reducing stiffness, and enhancing overall grip and wrist control.

form: Interlace your fingers with your arms in front of your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Rotate your wrists in a figure eight motion, focusing on achieving a full range of motion.
proTips: Start slowly and increase speed as comfortable.
Keep your shoulders relaxed throughout the movement.
commonMistakes: Don't use your entire arm; focus on isolating the movement to your wrists.
